replicates.citation: Nasruddin, Arnas, Faqih & Giannetti (2016), Makara J. Technol. 20(3) 132-138
replicates.note: Rebuilt from the equations and assumptions the paper states. No figure, table or dataset from the paper is reproduced; its reported values are used only to score this implementation.

reconstructions.evidence: reproduces the paper's 22-35% Pareto axis from its own reported COP range 0.40-0.65

reconstructions.what: compressor isentropic efficiency as a function of pressure ratio
reconstructions.resolution: not recoverable; eta_is treated as free and inverted

reconstructions.evidence: as printed, the paper's own reported optima cost 2.3-2.5x its own reported Pareto range

gates.name: Optimum mixture composition reproduced
gates.reason: our COP maximum sits at a composition-range endpoint for every mixture, worst gap 0.93 mass fraction. The paper selects composition by 'maximizing COP, provided that the carbon dioxide did not undergo crystallization and values capable of burning (flammability) of hydrocarbons were reduced' — it quantifies neither the crystallization limit nor the flammability criterion, so the selection rule cannot be reproduced from the paper. The reported optima are constrained choices whose constraints are not published.

gates.name: COP at the reported thermoeconomic optimum, within 0.05
Isentropic efficiency inverted from the reported COP agrees across all three mixtures, within 0.05
gates.reason: implied eta_is {'propane': 0.6415, 'ethane': 0.6486, 'ethylene': 0.6621}, spread 0.021. The paper states compression is 'expressed as a function of pressure ratio' but never gives the function, and the author no longer has it. Three independent mixtures agreeing this closely is evidence the cycle is right and that the compressor ran near eta_is 0.65.

gates.name: Annual cost falls inside the reported Pareto range
gates.reason: 3 of 3 inside band with the cascade coefficient taken as 2382.9 (propane $9,100 against $5,400-$9,100; ethane $8,498 against $5,200-$9,000; ethylene $8,287 against $5,100-$8,800). With the coefficient AS PRINTED (23829) every mixture costs 2.3-2.5x the paper's own reported range, so the printed equation does not reproduce the paper's own figures. Both numbers are published; the tenfold reduction is our inference, adopted with the author's agreement but not recoverable from his records.

gates.name: Mixture ranking is unchanged when all three are scanned at the same evaporation temperature
gates.reason: at a common T_EVAP of -80 C the best mixture is propane (0.675); the paper selects ethylene from scans taken at -80, -85 and -82 C respectively. Captions: Fig 3 -80, Fig 4 -85, Fig 5 -82.
